missions.title: Review OnionDAO spending estimate template
missions.description: We've pre-built the template. Chicago tax rates: 10.25% sales tax on food/bev, 19% hotel tax (highest in US), 9% amusement tax on concerts, 9% commercial lease tax on venues, $3/trip ground transportation tax. Open docs/economic-impact.md — the table is ready, you just need real dollar amounts from Dev to fill the [TBD] fields.

missions.title: Ask Dev for OnionDAO spending data
missions.description: Contact the OnionDAO organizer. Ask for: total venue costs, catering invoices, number of restaurant buyouts, estimated out-of-town attendees. We need real numbers for the economic impact report.

missions.title: Plug Dev's numbers into the tax revenue calculator
missions.description: Once you have real spending data from Dev, multiply: Food × 10.25%, Hotels × 19%, Concerts × 9%, Venue × 9%. Example: if catering was $50K over 30 days, that's $5,125 in sales tax alone. Hotel stays for 200 out-of-towners at $150/night × 19% = significant. The table in docs/economic-impact.md does the math — just fill in actuals.

missions.title: Review Choose Chicago research (already done)
missions.description: ALREADY RESEARCHED: Choose Chicago spends ~$40M/year (from new 19% hotel tax TID) on marketing, bid fees, and incentives to attract conventions. They offer: Convention Attraction Fund grants, room night rebates ($5/night for 100+ room blocks), bid fee coverage (e.g. $1M for DNC bid). Competitors: Las Vegas $457M/yr, Orlando $116M, LA $62M, San Diego $57M. OnionDAO came FOR FREE. Read the full analysis in docs/economic-impact.md, then move on to the next mission.

missions.title: Post the Chicago irony angle
missions.description: Post: 'Chicago just raised hotel taxes to 19% — highest in the US — to fund $40M/year attracting conventions. Then Illinois passes a crypto tax driving those events away. The left hand is spending to attract what the right hand taxes out of existence. #RepealDATA'
missions.script: Chicago just raised hotel taxes to 19% — highest in the US — to fund $40M/year attracting conventions. Then Illinois passes a crypto tax driving those events away. The left hand is spending to attract what the right hand taxes out of existence. #RepealDATA #SaveOnionDAO

missions.title: Email Choose Chicago about OnionDAO
missions.description: Contact Choose Chicago's partnerships team. Introduce OnionDAO as a month-long tech event that brought 400+ people. Ask about their event support programs. Frame it as: 'We want to keep bringing this event to Chicago but state policy is making it difficult.'

missions.title: Pitch Crain's Chicago Business on the irony angle
missions.description: Email Crain's business desk. Pitch: 'Chicago spending $40M to attract events while state taxes away the ones already here.' Attach the economic impact data. Crain's covers the intersection of Chicago business and policy.

missions.title: Get testimonials from Chicago businesses OnionDAO supported
missions.description: Contact 2-3 restaurants or venues that hosted OnionDAO events. Ask: 'How much revenue did OnionDAO bring you? Would you support keeping them in Chicago?' Written quotes are gold for the economic impact report.

missions.title: Draft the economic impact one-pager
missions.description: Using real numbers from Dev + restaurant testimonials + tax calculations, create a polished one-page economic impact summary. This becomes the centerpiece document for meetings with legislators.

missions.title: Post the SXSW comparison
missions.description: Post: 'OnionDAO could be Chicago's SXSW — a month-long tech event with free workshops, free food, 400+ attendees. Austin doesn't tax the tech industry that makes SXSW possible. Why is Illinois? #RepealDATA'
